chapter: Funerals, Mardi Gras and civil rights
title: How the jazz funeral tradition has not changed
summary: He describes the correct jazz funeral, dirges then joyful music, and says his band still does it right.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Jazz funerals: dirges, hot return, second line

blocks.x: How did you see the, talking about getting back to brass bands, one part, the funerals, how have the funerals changed over the years and the funeral traditions? Church organizations.

Well, the funeral traditions with my band, and I would say with the other musicians who do carry on the tradition and the true traditional playing of a jazz funeral has not changed. Church, what I've learned, I learned from those guys 40 years ago and 50 years ago. And what I heard as a kid also, and I'm still doing it and trying to do the same thing as far as jazz funeral. Jazz funeral is a celebration of life, the beginning of a new life. And it's an honorable thing to be buried with a true jazz funeral rendition of music and so forth. And if you want to stick to the tradition of being, doing dirges after you have the casket and the body, and then joyful music after you leave the cemetery. And then another music, such as just a little while to stay here or some kind of other sort of relatively up-tempo gospel to get to the place, to get to the church or the funeral. That's what I saw the old guy do. And that's what he played it. Even at some time, if the person was a military person, one trumpet player would always play taps after the funeral. And have ruffled drums, and the drummer would roll sort of with a handkerchief on top of it and so forth, so that it's muffled down. And so, I'm sorry, but the young musicians today don't want to do it or can't do it. But they could. Because it's a beautiful ceremony when it's done right.

And we have all, as of today, we have always been called upon, if somebody of a high dignitary dies, to do a jazz funeral. Because we do it right. As a matter of fact, we just did one last week. We buried this football team. They were 15-1. We buried the Jets.
Oh, okay. Oh, okay. Well, that's from the left field.
Maybe we've got somebody who can resurrect those people.
Maybe so. I hope they resurrect the Saints.
